title: Bridgewatch rollout playlist and post-release notes draft
body:
Purpose and scope:

This doc is the compact 'day-of' playlist and 72h rollout calendar for the Bridgewatch release. It combines a lightweight operations checklist, staffing heuristics, telemetry thresholds, canary cohort plan, and a draft of the post-release notes (internal + customer-facing skeleton). Intention: single-pane checklist for on-call, deploy conductor, SRE steward, and release owner.

High-level goals:
- Deploy Bridgewatch (v2026.03.0) with zero customer-impact within SLA targets.
- Validate canary performance against latency and error SLOs; watch for model-routing regressions.
- Keep rollback ladders short and predictable; prefer gradual traffic shifts with safety throttles.

Quick links (bookmark these before go-time):
- Jira board: REL-2026 (primary)
- Canary dashboard: /dashboards/bridgewatch-canary (Grafana)
- Runbook: /confluence/Bridgewatch-Runbook
- Slack channel: #releases-bridgewatch and #sre-ops
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/862

72-hour calendar (compact):
- T-72h: Final smoke on staging, preflight run (owner: Aisha). Artifacts: smoke report + perf baseline.
- T-48h: Rollout rehearsal (dry-run) with a 10% synthetic traffic blast. Confirm telemetry sampling. (owner: SRE steward)
- T-24h: Freeze non-critical merges. Confirm on-call roster and escalation ladder published. (owner: release manager)
- T-6h: Warm caches & KV prefix pre-seeding on primary nodes. Ensure model cache primed for top-50 prompts. (owner: infra)
- T-0: Start canary cohort 1 -> 1% traffic for 20 mins. Increase only on green. (owner: deploy conductor)
- T+40m: If green, shift to canary cohort 2 -> 5% for 30 mins.
- T+1h20m: If green, move to 20% for 60 mins with autoscaling observed.
- T+2h30m: If green, ramp to 50% then full (subject to final signoff).
- T+24h: Post-deploy telemetry digest and first-day retrospective.

Day-of checklist (compact, use checkboxes in the UI):
Pre-deploy (30–60m before T0):
- [ ] Announce quiet window in #product and #sales (template below).
- [ ] Confirm staffing: conductor, infra, SRE, QA floater, release owner, comms.
- [ ] Confirm fallbacks: capacity reserve (Dedicated fallback policy) at 30% throttle.
- [ ] Tag and snapshot related infra components (k8s, serving nodes).
- [ ] Run truncated smoke on prod-like subset (latency, tail p50/p95/p99).

Canary steps and acceptance criteria:
- Canary cohort 1 (1%): smoke OK, no increase in 5xx > 0.2% baseline, latency p95 < baseline*1.15, CPU/GPU utilization within allowance.
- Canary cohort 2 (5%): No error trend, model output quality checks pass on sampled prompt set (automated eval).
- Canary cohort 3 (20%): No regional skew, KV cache hit-rate stable (> 75%), no memory pressure alarms.
- Ramp to 50/100% only after explicit green from conductor + SRE.

Telemetry & signal thresholds (alert if any of these occur):
- Error budget burn: > 30% within 1 hour after ramp.
- 5xx rate spikes: absolute increase > 0.5% vs baseline for 15m sliding window.
- Latency: p95 > baseline * 1.25 for 10m.
- GPU OOM or repeated OOMs on a node: immediate rollback.
- Model routing fallback rate > 2% for 5m (indicates compatibility issues).
- Unusual reranking score drift for top 100 queries (quality regression detector).

Staffing heuristics and role responsibilities (short):
- Release owner (Aisha): final go/no-go, customer comms signoff, post-mortem owner.
- Deploy conductor (Liam): execute traffic shifts, maintain canary timeline, coordinate with SRE.
- SRE steward (Sophie): watch telemetry, approve ramps, own rollback if needed.
- Infra lead (Daniel): node health, cache warming, autoscaling knobs.
- QA floater (Maya): run sampled output checks and escalate content/regression finds.

Rollback ladder (short, tiered):
1) Pause traffic ramp and hold at last known-good cohort.
2) If regressions persist: route new traffic to fallback model variant (redwood:model-compat-2025) and keep canary at previous level.
3) If severe (customer impact / high error): rollback to previous stable revision (v2026.02.8) and open incident.
4) If infra-level failure: engage Dedicated fallback and failover region per region-fallback playbook.

Communication templates (short):
- Slack quick alert (ops): "[BRIDGEWATCH] Issue: <short-desc>. Impact: <customer-impact>. Action: holding ramps / rollback initiated. Pager: <link>. Owner: <name>."
- Customer-facing blurb (support & comms draft): "We rolled out an update to Bridgewatch; some customers may see transient increases in latency for specific requests. We're actively rolling back affected traffic and will share an update in the next 30 minutes."

Post-release notes (internal draft, to be polished for public):
- Release: Bridgewatch v2026.03.0
- Date: 2026-03-14
- Summary: Improvements to model routing, KV cache prefetch, and reduced p99 latency for streaming responses. Introduces canary-aware autoscaling policy and a new telemetry sampling layer for prompt-level quality checks.
- Notable changes:
  - Model routing: added soft-fallback lanes and a compatibility shim for quantized variants.
  - Serving runtime: KV prefix prefetch to reduce cold-kv misses ~+0.18ms/token on avg.
  - Observability: endpoint-level sampling for model output checks + auto-eval triggers.
- Impact: Expected lower tail latency and fewer cold starts. No customer action required. If you notice unexpected behavior, contact support with trace id.
- Rollout notes: Gradual 1 -> 5 -> 20 -> 50 -> 100% over ~3 hours with safety throttles.

Post-deploy checks (T+1h, T+6h, T+24h):
- T+1h: Confirm no sustained SLO breaches, sample-run quality checks, commit deploy annotations.
- T+6h: Internal retrospective notes, capture any uncovered issues, collect perf deltas.
- T+24h: Publish short postmortem if any rollback; otherwise publish rollout digest and customer notes.

Open questions / TODOs before T0:
- Confirm synthetic prompt set covers top 80% of user intents (Maya).
- Ensure fallback model is warmed for each region (Daniel).
- Get signoff from product for customer-facing blurb (Aisha).

Notes to self (informal):
- If we see model-quality drift, default to routing back to older quantized variant rather than infra rollback; avoids cache warm-up penalty.
- Keep an eye on cross-region latencies — sometimes a subtle routing mismatch shows only after 20% ramp.

Revision history:
- 2026-03-14: initial sketch (Aisha).
- 2026-03-16: added telemetry thresholds and staffing heuristics after dry-run (Sophie, Daniel).

Attachments to add before final:
- Final smoke report (staging)
- Canary dashboard snapshot (t-1h)
- Customer comms signoff thread link

End of doc.
